executive_summary: AI-assisted security research has surfaced a nine-year-old zero-day in the Linux kernel, affecting a broad swath of distributions with no patch yet available — elevating risk across Linux-dependent infrastructure while remediation timelines remain unknown.

CISA has added a newly confirmed actively exploited vulnerability to its KEV catalog, triggering mandatory remediation deadlines for federal agencies and raising immediate action requirements for MSPs serving regulated clients under BOD 22-01.

A multi-source-confirmed state-sponsored campaign deploying the 'Deep#Door' multi-stage backdoor has been identified, featuring advanced evasion techniques and TTPs consistent with known APT tooling targeting espionage and operational disruption objectives.

Two U.S. cybersecurity professionals have been sentenced to federal prison for providing operational support to a ransomware gang, establishing a significant legal precedent for insider threat accountability within the security industry itself.

Anthropic has launched 'Claude Security,' an LLM-native vulnerability scanning tool targeting developer environments and CI/CD pipeline integration, signaling an accelerating shift toward AI-augmented security tooling across the vulnerability management lifecycle.

cyber_news.title: Nine-Year-Old Zero-Day in Linux Kernel Uncovered Using AI-Assisted Research
cyber_news.summary: AI-assisted security research has uncovered a zero-day vulnerability that has existed undetected in the Linux kernel for approximately nine years, affecting a broad range of Linux distributions. The flaw carries elevated active-exploit risk and has drawn cross-source coverage given the scope of potentially affected infrastructure. Patch availability remains pending across major distribution maintainers.
cyber_news.expanded: The vulnerability was identified through an AI-augmented code analysis pipeline capable of reasoning over large volumes of kernel source history — a technique that outpaced traditional static analysis by correlating subtle semantic patterns across years of commits. The flaw itself resides in a kernel subsystem present across mainstream distributions including derivatives of Red Hat, Debian, Ubuntu, and SUSE, meaning the attack surface spans server, cloud, and embedded Linux deployments simultaneously. Because the vulnerability has existed since approximately 2017, any Linux system updated through normal patch cycles over the past nine years would still carry the flaw — the absence of a CVE assignment during that window means no automated patch management solution would have flagged it. Exploit complexity and required privilege levels have not been fully disclosed pending coordinated distro disclosure.

cyber_news.title: Deep#Door Backdoor Campaign: Sophisticated State-Sponsored Espionage and Disruption Toolkit Identified
cyber_news.summary: A newly identified multi-stage backdoor tracked as 'Deep#Door' has been confirmed across four independent threat intelligence sources, indicating an active state-sponsored campaign targeting espionage and operational disruption. The implant demonstrates advanced evasion capabilities with TTP overlaps to known APT tooling clusters. SecurityWeek, Dark Reading, The Hacker News, and Talos Intelligence have all independently reported on the campaign within the current briefing cycle.
cyber_news.expanded: Deep#Door operates as a staged loader architecture — initial access is followed by a lightweight first-stage dropper that performs environment fingerprinting before pulling a fully featured second-stage implant from attacker-controlled infrastructure, reducing detection surface during initial compromise. The backdoor employs process hollowing and DLL side-loading for persistence, injecting into legitimate signed Windows processes to evade behavioral EDR heuristics. Command-and-control communications are routed over encrypted channels mimicking legitimate HTTPS traffic to cloud service provider endpoints, complicating network-layer detection. Attribution indicators overlap with tooling previously associated with at least one nation-state threat cluster known for targeting government contractors and critical infrastructure operators, though full attribution has not been publicly confirmed.

cyber_news.title: Two U.S. Security Professionals Convicted and Sentenced for Material Support of Ransomware Operation
cyber_news.summary: Two individuals with active cybersecurity backgrounds were sentenced to federal prison after providing operational security consulting and tooling to a ransomware criminal organization. The case represents a meaningful legal precedent for insider threat liability and professional accountability in the security industry. Both defendants used their legitimate industry knowledge to assist threat actors in evading law enforcement and improving operational security.
cyber_news.expanded: The prosecution successfully argued that the defendants' industry expertise constituted material support rather than incidental contact, with evidence including direct advisory communications on avoiding attribution, guidance on cryptocurrency laundering tradecraft, and provision of tooling components. The case is notable because both individuals maintained active professional identities in the security community during the period of their cooperation with the ransomware group — illustrating the insider threat vector originating not from disgruntled employees but from financially motivated professionals exploiting privileged knowledge. Federal sentencing guidelines for cybercrime material support were applied, and the DOJ's public statements explicitly framed the prosecution as a deterrent signal to the security practitioner community. The case is likely to influence both hiring background check standards and ethics policy enforcement at MSPs and MSSPs with privileged access to client environments.

cyber_news.title: CISA KEV Updated: Newly Confirmed Actively Exploited Vulnerability Added to Catalog
cyber_news.summary: CISA has confirmed the addition of a newly observed actively exploited vulnerability to the Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog, triggering mandatory remediation windows for federal agencies under Binding Operational Directive 22-01. MSPs serving government or regulated clients should treat this as a Priority 1 remediation item. The specific CVE identifier should be verified directly at the CISA KEV catalog, as the full technical disclosure was not available in the feed summary at time of processing.
cyber_news.expanded: CISA's KEV addition process requires confirmation of active exploitation in the wild — meaning this is not a theoretical risk but an observed, weaponized vulnerability currently being leveraged by threat actors. BOD 22-01 mandates that Federal Civilian Executive Branch agencies remediate KEV-listed vulnerabilities within defined windows (typically 2 weeks for critical, though timelines vary by CVE). For MSPs, KEV additions serve as authoritative exploitation signal that should immediately elevate any corresponding vulnerability from routine patching queues to emergency remediation workflows regardless of CVSS score. The CISA KEV addition may be associated with the broader exploitation activity implied by other stories in this briefing cycle — cross-referencing with the Linux kernel zero-day and Deep#Door campaign IOCs is recommended.

cyber_news.title: Anthropic Launches Claude-Powered Security Tool for AI-Native Vulnerability Scanning
cyber_news.summary: Anthropic has released 'Claude Security,' an LLM-native security capability designed to identify code-level vulnerabilities and configuration weaknesses by applying large language model reasoning to static analysis problems. The initial release targets developer environments and CI/CD pipeline integration, positioning it as a complement or competitor to existing SAST and DAST tooling. The launch signals continued acceleration of AI integration into the vulnerability management lifecycle.
cyber_news.expanded: Unlike traditional SAST tools that rely on deterministic rule sets or pattern matching against known vulnerability signatures, Claude Security applies semantic reasoning to understand code intent — enabling detection of logical flaws, authentication bypasses, and business-logic vulnerabilities that signature-based scanners routinely miss. The CI/CD integration model means vulnerability findings surface during the development pipeline rather than post-deployment, shifting left in a manner consistent with DevSecOps methodology. Early documentation suggests the tool can contextualize findings within the surrounding codebase to reduce false-positive rates, a historically significant pain point for SAST adoption. For MSPs offering vCISO or security advisory services, the emergence of LLM-augmented scanning tools will require updating service delivery frameworks and client-facing vulnerability assessment methodologies.

cyber_news.title: Microsoft Patches Remote Desktop Bug That Suppressed or Misrepresented Certificate Security Warnings
cyber_news.summary: Microsoft has issued a patch for a Remote Desktop Protocol bug that caused security warning dialogs to display incorrectly — in certain configurations suppressing or misrepresenting certificate validation warnings that should alert users to untrusted RDP hosts. The flaw could have led users to establish RDP sessions to attacker-controlled or misconfigured hosts without receiving proper security notification. The fix applies to Windows environments with RDP gateway configurations.
cyber_news.expanded: The bug affected the client-side certificate warning presentation layer in RDP, meaning that in affected configurations a man-in-the-middle or rogue RDP endpoint could complete a session handshake without triggering the expected 'The identity of the remote computer cannot be verified' warning dialog. This is particularly significant in SMB-managed environments where RDP is frequently used for remote administration and end-user remote work — both scenarios where users may not have the baseline security literacy to question a missing warning. The post-patch verification step is non-trivial: MSPs should actively test that warning dialogs appear correctly on RDP gateway configurations rather than assuming the patch alone restores expected behavior, as misconfigured certificate trust stores could persist the issue independently of the software bug.

cyber_news.title: Active Phishing Campaign Exploits Trusted SaaS Platforms to Bypass Secure Email Gateways
cyber_news.summary: Threat actors are actively abusing legitimate SaaS platforms — including file-sharing services and form-builder tools — to host phishing lures that bypass reputation-based secure email gateway filters by leveraging the trusted sending domains of the abused platforms. The technique sidesteps conventional email security tooling by ensuring the delivery infrastructure itself carries a high-reputation score. The campaign has been observed across multiple overlapping threat intelligence sources this cycle.
cyber_news.expanded: The attack chain begins with lure emails sent from legitimate SaaS platform notification addresses (e.g., a form submission alert from a known collaboration tool), directing targets to attacker-created content hosted within those platforms' own domains. Because the email originates from and links to infrastructure with established positive sender reputation, both email authentication checks (SPF, DKIM, DMARC) and URL reputation filters pass the message. The hosted phishing page typically mimics Microsoft 365 or VPN login portals, with session cookie harvesting capability to capture post-MFA authenticated sessions rather than just static credentials. This technique is increasingly effective against organizations that have invested heavily in email gateway technology, as it deliberately targets the implicit trust those systems extend to major cloud platforms — a trust that cannot be revoked without also blocking legitimate business communications from those same services.

cyber_news.title: New Infostealer Variant Specifically Targets Browser-Stored Credentials and Software MFA Tokens
cyber_news.summary: A newly documented infostealer variant is actively circulating with specific functionality to extract saved credentials, session cookies, and software-based TOTP MFA tokens from browsers, with delivery primarily via malvertising and cracked software distribution channels. The variant has been observed targeting accounts protected by app-based MFA, directly undermining a common SMB-tier authentication control. Both BleepingComputer and Talos Intelligence have reported on the same underlying variant.
cyber_news.expanded: The infostealer's browser targeting module iterates across Chrome, Firefox, Edge, and Brave credential stores, extracting both saved passwords from the browser's encrypted vault and active session cookies that represent authenticated post-MFA sessions — meaning attackers can replay sessions without needing to perform the MFA challenge at all. The TOTP extraction component reads the shared secret seeds stored by software authenticator browser extensions (such as Authenticator.cc or similar), enabling the attacker to generate valid one-time codes independently. Delivery via malvertising is particularly difficult to block at scale because the ads appear on legitimate high-traffic sites through compromised ad network inventory. The combination of credential, session, and TOTP seed theft in a single payload represents a materially more complete account takeover capability than first-generation stealers that targeted only static credentials.

cyber_news.title: Palo Alto Unit 42: Living-Off-the-Land Binary Abuse Surging Across Observed Intrusions
cyber_news.summary: Palo Alto Unit 42 has published research documenting a notable increase in living-off-the-land binary (LoLBin) abuse across recently observed intrusion campaigns, with attackers chaining legitimate Windows system utilities to maintain persistence and enable lateral movement while evading signature-based endpoint detection. The trend reflects deliberate attacker adaptation to widespread EDR deployment across enterprise and managed environments. Utilities including mshta, certutil, wmic, and rundll32 are featured prominently in observed chains.
cyber_news.expanded: The LoLBin technique exploits the fundamental tension in EDR design: legitimate system binaries must be permitted to execute, but their behavior can be subverted to carry out attacker objectives. In observed intrusion chains, attackers are stringing multiple LoLBins sequentially — for example, using certutil to download a payload, mshta to execute it via an HTA file, and rundll32 to load a malicious DLL into a trusted process — such that no single execution event appears unambiguously malicious in isolation. The Unit 42 research notes that detection requires correlation of behavioral sequences rather than individual process events, demanding SIEM rules and EDR behavioral policies tuned for multi-step LoLBin chains rather than single-binary abuse signatures. The LOLBAS Project (lolbas-project.github.io) documents the full catalog of abusable binaries and should be treated as a required reference for tuning detection coverage.

cyber_news.title: CrowdStrike Research: Ransomware Groups Adopting Intermittent Encryption to Compress Attack Windows
cyber_news.summary: CrowdStrike has documented a tactical shift among ransomware operators toward intermittent encryption — partially encrypting file contents rather than performing full-file encryption — in order to reduce execution time and evade behavioral detection systems that trigger on sustained high-volume write activity. The approach meaningfully compresses the defender response window between initial encryption activity and file system impact. The technique has been observed across multiple ransomware families tracked by CrowdStrike this quarter.
cyber_news.expanded: Traditional ransomware detection heuristics on endpoint protection platforms commonly rely on detecting anomalous volume of file modifications or entropy spikes across the file system — both of which intermittent encryption intentionally reduces. By encrypting only the first 10-20% of each file (sufficient to render the file unrecoverable without the key), ransomware operators achieve the same extortion leverage while cutting execution time by an order of magnitude and staying below volume-based behavioral detection thresholds. The compressed attack timeline also reduces the effectiveness of automated IR playbook triggers that depend on detection-to-response latency assumptions built around full-encryption campaigns. Security teams should validate that their endpoint protection platform's ransomware detection logic is not solely dependent on encryption volume or entropy analysis, and that backup and snapshot systems have sufficiently granular recovery point objectives to survive an attack that may complete before automated response initiates.

deep_dive.title: Deep#Door Backdoor: Multi-Stage State-Sponsored Espionage and Disruption Campaign
deep_dive.content: Deep#Door is a sophisticated multi-stage backdoor implant confirmed by four independent threat intelligence sources — SecurityWeek, Dark Reading, The Hacker News, and Talos Intelligence — in the current briefing cycle, making it the most broadly corroborated threat story this period. The campaign exhibits hallmarks of state-sponsored development: a staged loader architecture that separates initial access from full implant deployment to minimize early-stage detection exposure, process hollowing and DLL side-loading for persistence within legitimate signed Windows processes, and C2 communications tunneled over HTTPS to cloud provider infrastructure to evade network-layer inspection. Initial access tradecraft has not been fully disclosed, but TTP overlaps with previously attributed APT tooling suggest spearphishing or supply-chain staging as likely vectors. The first-stage dropper performs environment fingerprinting — checking for sandbox indicators, domain membership, and installed security tooling — before pulling the second-stage payload, meaning the full implant may never deploy in sandboxed analysis environments, complicating automated detection. The second stage provides full RAT capability including file exfiltration, keylogging, screenshot capture, and a disruptive module consistent with pre-positioned sabotage capability. MITRE ATT&CK-relevant techniques span Initial Access (T1566), Execution (T1055 — Process Injection), Persistence (T1574 — DLL Side-Loading), Defense Evasion (T1036 — Masquerading), and Exfiltration (T1041). Attribution indicators overlap with a known nation-state cluster targeting government contractors, defense industrial base organizations, and critical infrastructure operators. MSP SOC teams should immediately deploy available IOCs into EDR and SIEM platforms, prioritize threat hunting for staged loader activity in telemetry from the past 30–60 days, and update detection rules to cover the identified DLL side-loading and process hollowing chains.
